summary: China has unilaterally opened visa-free entry of up to 30 days to ordinary-passport holders of 50 countries — including many EU members, the UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and South Korea — while US and Indian citizens still need an embassy visa; a separate 240-hour (10-day) visa-free transit scheme covers 57 nationalities passing through to a third country.

currencyLimits.text: Chinese Customs requires you to declare RMB 20,000 or more in cash, or foreign currency in cash worth US$5,000 or more, on arrival and on departure; no more than RMB 20,000 may be brought in or taken out.

notes: Canada's travel advice says Chinese immigration officials take and keep the fingerprints of travellers aged 14 to 70 on entry, with some exceptions.

Canada's travel advice says there are absolute prohibitions on importing arms, drugs, and plant or animal products that could carry disease or pests, and restrictions on printed material, film, photos and recordings considered detrimental to China's interests.
The UK Foreign Office says the import, possession and use of drones are strictly regulated; contact the Civil Aviation Administration of China before travel.

payments.text: The UK Foreign Office says cashless payments through apps such as WeChat or Alipay are almost universal, and that outside major cities credit cards are not always accepted and ATMs are limited. Canada's travel advice says these platforms let foreign travellers link an international credit card, that international cards are accepted in many hotels and larger establishments but not universally, and that using foreign currency for everyday transactions is illegal.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says serious crime against foreign nationals is relatively rare, but incidents can happen; Canada adds that petty crime such as pickpocketing and phone theft occurs and that criminals target foreigners, especially in major cities and tourist areas. The UK warns that foreign nationals involved in business or civil disputes can be stopped from leaving by an exit ban.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says major Chinese payment platforms let foreign travellers link an international credit card and pay by scanning QR codes in shops, restaurants, taxis and on public transport, and advises following the platform's official setup instructions; the UK Foreign Office says such app payments are almost universal.

The UK Foreign Office and Canada say you must register your place of residence with the local Public Security Bureau within 24 hours of arrival. Hotels do it at check-in; if you stay in a private home you must register yourself. Canada says failure can lead to fines or detention.

The UK Foreign Office says the Chinese authorities control internet access and some services are permanently blocked, including Google, Facebook, YouTube and X; others may sometimes be blocked. It adds that VPNs must be licensed by the Chinese government.

Even if your passport needs a visa for China, the 240-hour (10-day) visa-free transit lets eligible nationalities — including US, Mexican and Indonesian citizens — visit without a visa when arriving at an eligible port and continuing to a different country or region.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for China?
faq.answer: Yes, for a regular visit US citizens need a tourist (L) visa, which costs 140 USD at the Chinese Embassy in the US. However, US passport holders transiting to a third country can use the 240-hour (10-day) visa-free transit policy at eligible ports instead.

faq.question: Which nationalities can visit China visa-free?
faq.answer: China's Foreign Ministry lists 50 countries whose ordinary-passport holders can visit visa-free for up to 30 days, including many EU members (Germany, France, Spain, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland and others), Switzerland, Ireland, the UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Brazil and Russia. It is announced as in force until December 31, 2026 (Russia until December 31, 2027; Brunei with no end date).

faq.question: How does China's 240-hour visa-free transit work?
faq.answer: Citizens of 57 countries — including the US, UK, Canada and Mexico — can enter without a visa for up to 240 hours (10 days) at any of 65 eligible ports in 24 provinces when they hold an ordinary passport and an onward ticket with a fixed date and itinerary to a third country or region. Travel is limited to the permitted regions.

faq.question: Can I pay with my foreign card in China?
faq.answer: Not everywhere. Canada's travel advice says international credit cards are accepted in many hotels and larger establishments but not universally, and that major payment platforms let foreign travellers link an international card to pay by QR code. The UK Foreign Office says outside major cities cards are not always accepted and ATMs are limited.

faq.question: Do I have to register with the police in China?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK Foreign Office and Canada say you must register your place of residence with the local Public Security Bureau within 24 hours of arrival. Hotels do this at check-in; if you stay with family or friends in a private home you must register yourself, and Canada says failure can result in fines or detention.
